welcome.title: Nuz-guide
welcome.text:
Pick a section to read the rules, check your score or find out what's changed in Kaizo Baconmon.

A selects and turns the page. B goes back in menus. Choose Close to return to the game.

bacon_intro.title: Ironmon, but tastier
bacon_intro.text:
I made Kaizo Baconmon as a quality-of-life take on Kaizo Ironmon: Ironmon, but tastier.

Some changes are based on or inspired by Ironmon VS, with a few extra conveniences I wanted for my own runs. It keeps the Kaizo challenge, with less fiddling between fights.

I implemented the following changes from core Kaizo Ironmon:

- Start in Oak's lab after choosing your gender, name and rival's name. The opening rival battle still happens at level 8.

- Choose Classic or Modern at the start. Classic keeps Gen III battles. Modern adds the physical/special move split and updates existing abilities. It does not add abilities, learnsets or BST changes.

- Pick a starter ball before seeing the choices and keep that same position across runs. Your chosen starter is legal regardless of BST. This replaces normal starter selection. It does not allow over-limit wild pivots.

- Start with a Master Ball and five Poke Balls for legal catches.

- Early encounters rotate as they do in Ironmon VS.

- Use field HMs without teaching them or carrying an HM friend. You still need the HM, badge and normal story prerequisites. Fly from the Town Map.

- Rock Tunnel is already lit, so you do not need Flash to see there.

- Use the Move Reminder in the Move Deleter's Fuchsia house. Each successful relearn costs one TM of your choice. The usual Sketch restriction still applies.

- Use Oak's lab machine to maximise or plummet your runner's friendship. The former friendship helpers point you there.

- Use the Viridian Forest nurse even when poisoned. Dungeon beds and other optional dungeon healers remain banned.

- Chance-based hidden items are guaranteed to appear at their normal refresh. Collect each renewable location once; farming is still banned.

- Track progress with the 33-point VS-style score and dungeon-clear log. A dungeon bonus requires all its trainers in one visit without optional Center-equivalent healing.

- Press L while choosing an attack to read its description. Move summaries show physical, special and status symbols.

- A Baconmon title screen starring Grumpig.

- Start with Nuz-guide: the complete Baconmon rules, other challenge formats, mode details, scoring, credits and ROM information.

Everything else follows the full Kaizo Baconmon rules in this guide. Built-in conveniences do not waive the remaining restrictions.

bacon_starter.title: Starter and pivots
bacon_starter.text:
Use one Pokemon in battle. No backups, switching between runners, sacrifice Pokemon or extra party abilities. This ROM does not need HM friends. Do not keep extra Pokemon for Pickup, weather, item bonuses or any other advantage.

Obtain no more than six Pokemon during the run, counting your starter and accepted pivots. You may accept at most one Pokemon from each named route or area. It need not be the first encounter. Gifts and static encounters also use that area's allowance. Separate floors of one named dungeon do not create extra catches.

A catch may be at most four levels above your current runner. Commit to a pivot when you catch it, before examining its stats, moves or ability. Permanently retire the old runner; you cannot return to it later. Do not catch several candidates and compare them.

You may immediately box an unwanted catch without viewing any stats or moves and continue as if it had not been accepted. This is not permission to scout caught Pokemon or use a second battler. Throwing a ball to escape a dangerous wild encounter is allowed.

Do not deliberately knock out wild Pokemon for experience. Scout or run instead. A wild Pokemon destroying itself is not deliberate training. If you accidentally knock one out while scouting, you must pivot to a legal catch from that area before leaving or healing. If that cannot be done legally, the run cannot continue.

bacon_helpers.title: Baconmon helpers
bacon_helpers.text:
The lab machine changes only your lead Pokemon's friendship. Maximise sets it to 255. Plummet sets it to 0. Cancel changes nothing. It is not a healing machine.

The lab aide and both Viridian friendship helpers now direct you to the lab machine. Talking to them does not change friendship.

The Viridian Forest nurse restores the party and clears poison. You can use her outside a dungeon attempt. Leaving Mt. Moon to visit her and then returning does not count as a clean Mt. Moon clear.

The Move Reminder sits opposite the Move Deleter in Fuchsia. Pick a forgotten move from the list. Your payment TM is his fee; the move on it doesn't matter.

Choose the TM you are willing to lose. It is removed only after a move is successfully remembered. Cancelling, choosing an Egg or having no eligible moves costs nothing. HMs are not payment.

Paying with an otherwise unusable TM is allowed in Baconmon. Teaching an ordinary found or bought TM is still restricted by Kaizo rules. Do not use the reminder to repeat Sketch after it has copied a move.

bacon_healing.title: Healing and dungeon entries
bacon_healing.text:
Use HP, status and PP recovery items only during battle. Do not use them from the Bag outside battle. PP Up and PP Max are allowed outside battle. Found vitamins and evolution stones are not recovery items.

Pokemon Centers and equivalent healers are allowed outside dungeons. Baconmon also allows the Viridian Forest nurse, including when poisoned. Forests are not dungeons. The lab machine changes friendship only and does not restore HP, status or PP.

Enter a gym or dojo ready to defeat every trainer. You may not leave until all of them are beaten. No optional Center-equivalent healing inside.

Enter each other dungeon once unless the story requires another visit. Dungeons include caves, hideouts and buildings containing trainers. You may skip optional trainers in an ordinary dungeon, but skipped trainers mean no full-clear bonus. Leaving before completion does not grant permission to return for them.

Do not use dungeon healing stations, including the S.S. Anne bed, Silph bed or an NPC doing the same job as a Center. A forced story heal is allowed; returning voluntarily for another is not.

For a scored full clear, defeat all required trainer groups in one continuous visit without optional Center-equivalent healing. Floors, internal lifts and Silph warp tiles stay within that visit. Leaving, healing and returning forfeits the bonus and breaks the one-entry rule unless that return is story-required. Legal in-battle recovery items do not spoil a clean clear.

bacon_travel.title: HMs and travel
bacon_travel.text:
Keep the required HM in your Bag and earn the badge that unlocks it. Interact with the obstacle as normal. Your runner does not need to know the move.

Cut needs the Cascade Badge. Fly needs the Thunder Badge. Surf needs the Soul Badge. Strength needs the Rainbow Badge. Flash needs the Boulder Badge. Rock Smash needs the Marsh Badge. Waterfall needs the Volcano Badge.

Other normal checks still matter: have a Pokemon, use the move in a suitable place and meet story or location requirements. This is not permission to skip progression.

Use the Town Map outdoors to choose an unlocked Fly destination. It works from the Bag or as a registered item. You still need HM02 and the Thunder Badge.

Rock Tunnel's two floors are lit. You do not need Flash to see there. That does not turn every other HM or badge check off.

HMs remain banned as battle moves under the inherited Ultimate rules. Removing the need to teach one does not make Surf, Strength or Fly a legal attack for Kaizo.

bacon_faq.title: Baconmon questions
bacon_faq.text:
Classic keeps Gen III battles. Modern adds the move split and the ability changes listed in the mode pages. Both use the same seed.

You can use the forest nurse, including with poison. You cannot leave an unfinished dungeon to heal and return, or use the Silph bed during a clear.

The Move Reminder takes one TM after a successful relearn. You still need to follow Kaizo's restrictions on teaching ordinary TMs.

Guaranteed hidden-item spawns don't change the no-farming rule. Collect each renewable location once.

The other directory entries explain different challenges. Choose their rules before starting and keep any extra requirements or records they need.

classic.title: Classic mode
classic.text:
Classic keeps FireRed's Gen III battle rules. Damaging moves use Attack or Special Attack according to their type, not according to the individual move.

Physical types are Normal, Fighting, Flying, Poison, Ground, Rock, Bug, Ghost and Steel. Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Psychic, Ice, Dragon and Dark are special.

A Dark move such as Bite is special in Classic. Ghost attacks such as Shadow Ball are physical. Status moves still use their own effects rather than a damage category.

Classic keeps the original ability effects. Sturdy blocks one-hit knockout moves; it does not protect a full-health Pokemon from an ordinary lethal hit.

You still get Baconmon's lab start, helpers, field HM access, light Rock Tunnel, TM-paid reminder, guide and other changes that are not battle-mode changes.

The seed's species, stat totals, randomized stat spread, types, abilities and learnsets remain that seed's data. Choosing Classic does not reroll them.

modern_split.title: Modern: move split
modern_split.text:
In Modern, each damaging move has its own physical or special category. Bite is physical, Shadow Ball is special, and Hyper Beam is special. Status moves have a separate symbol.

The move's category chooses Attack and Defense, or Special Attack and Special Defense. A randomized move type does not change that move's modern category.

Reflect and Light Screen follow the move category. Counter, Mirror Coat, Hustle's physical accuracy check and the relevant damage handling use the split too.

Fire and Ice attacks can be physical. Weather, Flash Fire and Thick Fat follow the applicable move category.

Hidden Power and Weather Ball still work out their changing type through their normal effects, but remain special attacks in Modern. Their type change is not a switch to physical damage.

Move-category symbols are shown in the summary screen and the battle move-information panel. Press L while choosing a move to read the description. Use the D-pad to browse; L or B closes the panel.

Note: Fairy typing is intentionally omitted.

modern_a.title: Modern abilities: A-F
modern_a.text:
Color Change waits until the final hit of a multi-hit move before changing the target's type.

Compound Eyes keeps its accuracy boost and improves wild held-item rolls. The common and rare slots use the modern 60% and 20% thresholds when the lead ability applies, instead of the usual 50% and 5% slots.

Drizzle starts five turns of rain. This does not shorten weather coming from a map or another permanent field effect.

Drought starts five turns of sunlight. Sand Stream uses the same five-turn rule for its sandstorm.

Effect Spore has a 30% total chance on eligible contact and does not affect a Grass-type attacker. The result can be sleep, poison or paralysis.

Static, Poison Point and Cute Charm use 30% contact chances instead of the original one-in-three checks. Their normal eligibility and immunity checks still apply.

Flash Fire responds to Fire moves, including status Fire moves, without the old frozen-user restriction. Its Fire damage bonus is applied to the appropriate move category.

modern_b.title: Modern abilities: I-O
modern_b.text:
Illuminate has Keen Eye's battle protection here: it prevents accuracy drops and ignores a target's positive evasion stages. This does not make Rock Tunnel dark again.

Inner Focus prevents flinching and blocks Intimidate's Attack drop.

Keen Eye prevents accuracy drops and ignores positive evasion stages. Other accuracy modifiers still matter.

Lightning Rod redirects eligible Electric moves, including an ally's move in doubles. It absorbs Electric moves and raises Special Attack by one stage, up to the usual limit.

Oblivious blocks attraction, Taunt and Intimidate. Gaining the ability also clears an active Taunt here.

Own Tempo blocks confusion and Intimidate. It does not prevent unrelated Attack drops from other sources.

These are updates to abilities already present in Gen III. They do not add later abilities or change which ability a species has in the seed.

modern_c.title: Modern abilities: P-Z
modern_c.text:
Pickup can recover an eligible berry or herb consumed earlier in the turn. The Pokemon needs an empty held-item slot.

Plus and Minus work with a living doubles partner that has either Plus or Minus. The partner does not have to have the opposite ability.

Rough Skin removes one eighth of the contact attacker's maximum HP, rather than the old one sixteenth.

Shadow Tag does not trap another Shadow Tag user. Ghost types also get the modern escape protection against trapping abilities.

Stench gives eligible damaging attacks a 10% flinch chance. It does not stack with the flinch-granting held-item effect handled by that routine.

Sturdy lets a full-health Pokemon survive an otherwise lethal direct hit with 1 HP. Later hits and residual damage can still finish it. It also works against confusion self-damage.

Synchronize reflects bad poison as bad poison instead of downgrading it to ordinary poison.

Trace avoids copying no ability, Trace or Forecast. It otherwise uses the native eligible-target logic.

Volt Absorb and Water Absorb can activate on the matching type's status moves as well as damaging moves. Thick Fat's Fire and Ice reduction follows the split.

modern_limits.title: What Modern does not change
modern_limits.text:
Modern changes move categories and the ability effects listed here. Seed data stays unchanged: Pokemon, types, abilities, items, BSTs and learnsets.

Move power, accuracy, PP and secondary effects still come from the seed. Other mechanics keep Gen III rules.

The Huge Power and Pure Power restriction still applies. Check the move's category symbol.

Use the same mode when comparing runs.

Note: Fairy typing is intentionally omitted.

nuz_basic.title: Basic Nuzlocke
nuz_basic.text:
Nick Franco's original challenge has two central rules: only the first encounter in each area is your catch, and a fainted Pokemon is permanently out of the run.

If that encounter is knocked out, flees or cannot be caught, the area is used up. Do not keep trying until you find a species you prefer.

Put fainted Pokemon in a clearly marked dead box or release them. Do not revive them for a difficult fight. Keeping them as a record is fine if they never return to active use.

Nicknaming every catch is a common addition, not one of the original two requirements. Other familiar rules, such as level caps and no battle items, are separate additions.

Decide how gifts, duplicate species and a full-party defeat work before you play. A rule agreed in advance is different from changing it to rescue a favourite.

Keep a record of your encounters and lost Pokemon. Box or release fainted Pokemon yourself.

nuz_areas.title: What counts as an area?
nuz_areas.text:
Use the game's named met location as your starting point. A new patch of grass on the same named route is usually not a new catch.

Decide whether a named cave counts once for the whole cave or once per separately named section. Do not invent floor-by-floor catches only after losing the first one.

Grass, surfing and fishing in the same area normally share one encounter. Choosing to fish first is a choice about that area's catch, not permission to catch once from each method.

An encounter caused by a tree, rock or another special method needs the same prior agreement. A change of encounter method is not automatically a new area.

Record the area when you catch the Pokemon, not when you later decide to use it. Storage does not restore a used encounter.

Ironmon works differently: its route catch can be chosen after scouting. Do not combine that freedom with Nuzlocke's rules by accident.

nuz_death.title: Fainting, loss and resets
nuz_death.text:
Fainting means the Pokemon is gone for that run, including in an ordinary trainer battle or while training. A reset cannot erase an unfavourable result.

Agree on what a full-party defeat means. A common rule ends the run on a wipe. Another allows rebuilding from living boxed Pokemon. Pick one beforehand.

No reserve can rescue a Kaizo Ironmon runner after it faints. The challenge uses a single runner, and that run is over.

Save states can be convenient for loading a fresh lab or recovering from an emulator problem. They are not extra lives or a way to reroll a battle.

If a genuine crash happens, restore the nearest sensible save and document what happened. In a competition, use the organiser's recovery policy.

A self-imposed challenge is yours to change for practice. Label that change honestly instead of presenting it as an unchanged ruleset.

hardcore.title: Hardcore Nuzlocke
hardcore.text:
A common Hardcore Nuzlocke adds three limits to a normal Nuzlocke: Set battle style, no Bag items during trainer battles, and level caps.

Set removes the free switch after an opponent faints. You can still switch on your turn and spend that turn doing it.

The battle-item rule normally permits held items and balls for a legal encounter. Agree on exceptions and forced tutorials before starting.

Set a cap using the next boss's highest-level Pokemon. Box any Pokemon that goes over the cap until the cap rises.

Decide how you handle levels gained during a boss fight and the Elite Four's different levels. Many runs check the cap at the start of each fight; others use a single entry cap.

Randomized trainer levels make a vanilla level chart unreliable. Know the event's cap convention before a blind run. Hardcore is a community rules family, not one universal tournament standard.

clauses_dupes.title: Duplicates clause
clauses_dupes.text:
A duplicates clause lets you skip an encounter that belongs to a species or evolution family you already caught. Decide whether the clause covers a species or its whole family.

Decide whether a Pokemon you lost still counts as owned for this rule. Also decide whether you stop after a fixed number of attempts or keep searching for something new.

Use the same duplicate rule for the whole run.

Without a duplicates clause, your first encounter can be another copy of something you already have. That is still a valid basic Nuzlocke.

clauses_shiny.title: Shiny clause
clauses_shiny.text:
A shiny clause is an optional exception for a shiny found after the area's normal encounter. Some players allow catching and using it; others allow the catch only as a keepsake.

Choose which version you mean before a shiny appears. A keepsake that was caught under a no-use exception should not suddenly join the team when a boss is difficult.

Do not deliberately raise shiny odds while claiming an unchanged challenge. A randomized colour palette is not a shiny.

Ironmon's published shiny allowance is different: a shiny can be a bonus wild knockout for experience. It is not a blanket extra-pivot clause. Read the selected Ironmon rules.

clauses_gifts.title: Gifts and static encounters
clauses_gifts.text:
A gift can use the area's normal encounter, count as a separate gift, or be banned. Static encounters can be treated the same way. Agree on one approach.

Your starter is usually a special allowance. A later gift is not automatically another starter allowance.

Trades commonly exchange one legal encounter for another Pokemon rather than creating an extra catch. Decide whether in-game trades are allowed before accepting one.

When two gifts share a named area, do not assume both are free. Check your chosen gift clause.

A forced story battle or a required capture can need an exception. State whether you may use that Pokemon afterward or must immediately box it.

clauses_hm.title: HM and progression exceptions
clauses_hm.text:
In an unmodified game, a run can reach a required HM obstacle without a living team member that can learn the move. Many players allow a helper for that obstacle only.

That helper must not battle, absorb a hit, supply a useful ability or create extra usable encounters unless the rules expressly permit it.

If it is forced into a fight, follow the agreed correction rule. Do not deliberately use it as a sacrifice.

Baconmon removes the need for that helper: own the HM, earn the badge and interact with the obstacle. You still need a Pokemon in the party and the normal location checks.

Check the event's rules before using a modified ROM in a race.

monotype.title: Monotype Nuzlocke
monotype.text:
Use a normal Nuzlocke with one chosen type. A common clause skips encounters that cannot legally join the type-restricted team.

Decide whether a Pokemon qualifies only while it currently has the type, or also if it will gain that type by evolution. Handle Pokemon that lose the type on evolution the same way.

Dual types normally qualify if one matches. Pick the type before seeing the available encounters.

In a type-randomized seed, use the seed's actual types if that is your agreement. Do not switch to vanilla types when doing so becomes convenient.

Do not call a free choice from every route a first-encounter Monolocke. State how the eligible-encounter exception works.

wedlocke.title: Wedlocke
wedlocke.text:
Marriland's Wedlocke makes pairs within the team. A Pokemon battles with its partner and can normally switch only to that partner, rather than to any of the six.

The original pairing approach uses opposite genders and a gender-based encounter exception to find partners. It also restricts freely boxing team members. Check Marriland's full rules for the detailed replacement cases.

Modern house versions may allow same-gender or genderless pairs. That is a stated variation, not a reason to change pairings in the middle of a fight.

If a partner faints, follow your chosen replacement and encounter rules. The living partner does not automatically become a free switch to the entire team.

Use a normal multi-Pokemon run for this. Kaizo Ironmon's single-runner restriction is a different challenge.

soullink.title: Soul Link
soullink.text:
Two players each run a Nuzlocke and link corresponding encounters as pairs. If one linked Pokemon dies, its partner is also permanently removed from the other run.

Agree on what makes a pair legal, how different areas line up between games and what happens if one player misses an encounter. Some versions also restrict duplicate primary types across the active teams.

Keep paired Pokemon active or boxed together according to your agreed rule. Moving one to the PC should not secretly break the link to avoid a death.

Use separate saves and coordinate catches. Ordinary FireRed does not manage the links for you.

Soul Link is a community challenge with many house versions. Write down yours rather than assuming another team's convention is universal.

smallteams.title: Littlelocke and baby limits
smallteams.text:
These names usually describe a Nuzlocke limited to unevolved or low-BST Pokemon. They do not always use the same eligibility list.

Decide whether a Pokemon must be able to evolve, whether single-stage species qualify, whether baby species are required, and what the BST limit is.

A Little Cup-inspired rule often bans species that cannot evolve. A low-BST run can allow them. Neither definition should be silently substituted for the other.

State how mandatory evolution is handled. Cancelling evolution is common in these runs but is not allowed under inherited Ultimate Ironmon rules.

If you use randomized stats, specify whether eligibility follows original BST or the current seed. Keep a written list when a name alone is unclear.

solo.title: Solo and no-evolution runs
solo.text:
A solo challenge uses one battler. It is not automatically a Nuzlocke: a normal solo run may permit fainting and ordinary reloading.

For a solo Nuzlocke, explicitly add permadeath and explain whether replacement encounters are allowed. Kaizo's pivot rules are one particular single-runner system.

A no-evolution run keeps Pokemon at their current stage. Decide whether catching evolved species is allowed or whether only first-stage catches qualify.

State what helper Pokemon can do. A helper that absorbs a hit or supplies Pickup is more than an HM carrier.

These are rule descriptions, not extra modes this item switches on. The ROM continues to allow normal party management.

randomizer.title: Randomizer Nuzlocke
randomizer.text:
Randomize a game, then follow the chosen Nuzlocke rules. Randomizing encounters alone is very different from randomizing types, abilities, moves, evolutions and trainer teams.

Record the settings and the seed if the tool provides them. Use the same settings when comparing attempts.

Choose a species-strength policy, move bans and evolution policy before starting. A randomizer preset does not decide those rules for you.

Keep a matching log for after the run if you want to review what could have happened. If the run is meant to be blind, do not read that log while playing.

Use BASE to make new Kaizo seeds. Run001 is a ready-made example; it stays the same each time you play it.

egglocke.title: Egglocke
egglocke.text:
Replace legal encounters with eggs from a prepared pool, often supplied by other people. The replacement takes the original encounter's place; it is not an extra catch.

Agree on levels, inherited moves, duplicate species, gender and illegal combinations before receiving the pool. Document how you make the hatchling fit the encounter's level.

Do not peek at every egg and choose the strongest unless that is the stated format. Use the agreed ordering or random selection.

Prepare and import your egg pool before starting.

wonderlocke.title: Wonderlocke
wonderlocke.text:
In games that support the feature, trade each legal encounter through Wonder Trade or its equivalent and use the received Pokemon as that encounter.

Agree on over-levelled returns, duplicates, eggs, hacked Pokemon and impossible moves. Re-trading an ineligible result needs a consistent rule.

Do not keep trading until a desirable result arrives. That defeats the random replacement unless the rejected returns were genuinely ineligible.

Wonder Trade requires a different game or a separate way to arrange the replacement Pokemon; FireRed has no online Wonder Trade.

genlocke.title: Generations run
genlocke.text:
Play a sequence of Nuzlockes across different games. Surviving champions can pass descendants or agreed successors into the next game.

Decide how many successors transfer, their starting levels and moves, and whether they consume early encounter slots. A descendant is not usually the original level-60 champion.

Record deaths across the whole series and state whether an evolution family becomes unavailable after a death.

Arrange the transfers and eggs between games separately.

draft.title: Draft and themed teams
draft.text:
Some runs restrict colours, body shapes, regions, habitats or a drafted species list. These are house formats; a theme name rarely supplies all the rules.

For an apocalyptic theme, define the surviving types or species first. For a chess-inspired team, assign each piece its allowed actions before it joins the party.

Keep the normal encounter and death rules unless you expressly replace them. A theme does not automatically grant a choice from every area.

Write down edge cases such as evolution changing a colour or a randomized type changing eligibility. Decide which source of species information you use.

planning.title: Before starting
planning.text:
Write down your ruleset, chosen clauses, battle mode, starter method, level caps and finish line. Agree on what counts as a loss.

Decide whether damage calculators, encounter lists and guides are allowed. A blind race and an open-information challenge are different formats.

Decide whether Rare Candies replace safe grinding. Some Nuzlockes allow that convenience; it is not permission to exceed a cap. Ordinary Kaizo does not grant free external candies.

Keep a normal save and backups for technical failures. Do not use backups to undo deaths, scout unseen outcomes or replay trainer battles.

For a race, use matching seeds, mode and rules. Agree on pauses, crashes and disputed results before the timer starts.

After a run, use the matching seed log to learn from it. Do not mistake an emulator diagnostic log for a randomizer's spoiler log.

iron_standard.title: Standard Ironmon
iron_standard.text:
Ironmon, created by iateyourpie, uses a randomized game and limits wild grinding. The first difficulty is Standard; later difficulties add restrictions.

The core catch rule allows one catch OR wild knockout per route, not necessarily the first encounter. Other experience is meant to come from trainers.

Fainting is permanent. A wiped party ends the run and the next attempt uses a newly randomized game. Do not salvage the held item from a dead Pokemon.

Shops are limited to balls and Repels. Found and gifted items supply the run. Buying something to exchange it for healing is still shopping for healing.

Declare up to three favourite species before a Gen III run. At most one may be legendary. A favourite appearing among the starters can override the random pick. Later games allow one extra favourite for each generation after Gen III.

Legendary, sub-legendary and mythical species are otherwise banned. Pseudo-legendaries are not automatically legendary. Evolving into a legendary is allowed. In ordinary Kaizo, a favourite legendary must still meet its strength limit.

Attempt the lab fight before resetting because you dislike the starter. Standard also asks you to speak to Mom at the beginning. Baconmon's direct lab start deliberately skips that opening errand.

Do not repeat trainers, farm renewable item locations or intentionally steal an item from a wild Pokemon you do not catch. Lucky Egg and Sacred Ash are banned.

Ultimate and Kaizo add more restrictions. Read those pages if you're playing either challenge.

iron_ultimate.title: Ultimate Ironmon
iron_ultimate.text:
Ultimate inherits Standard and adds Set battle style, a six-Pokemon total acquisition limit, mandatory evolution and stronger item restrictions.

HMs cannot be used as battle attacks. The published HM-friend exception is for necessary field access, not a spare battler or a useful passive ability.

A gym or dojo must be cleared without leaving. Dungeons have one visit, apart from required story returns. Forests are not classed as dungeons in this rule.

Use Fluctuating experience growth for ordinary species and Slow for legendaries. Set those growth rates in the randomizer. Leftovers, Soul Dew and Everstone join the item bans.

The six-Pokemon limit counts acquisitions across the whole run, not just the current party. A necessary HM friend after five of those six have been lost may only supply field access. Switch it out immediately if a forced-switch move brings it into battle. It cannot supply Pickup, healing or other advantages.

In FireRed, fight the S.S. Anne rival before other ship trainers. On the first Lavender visit, fight the tower rival before leaving town. Do not take Bill's early Sevii trip before the Elite Four.

Use the correct preset for your game.

kaizo_core.title: Kaizo: runner and catches
kaizo_core.text:
Kaizo adds a single runner to the inherited rules. A newly caught pivot permanently replaces it, and you commit before examining the new Pokemon's information.

No deliberate wild knockouts for training. Use the route's catch allowance to pivot. A wild Pokemon blowing itself up is not deliberate grinding.

The catch must be no more than four levels above your team's highest level. Catching something higher and promising to use it later is not the rule.

Pokemon with 599 BST or more are banned. An evolution taking a legal runner into a higher-BST species is allowed.

The favourite and nemesis clauses are specific predeclared exceptions, not a free choice of any starter after revealing them. Baconmon instead uses its fixed-ball rule and starter BST exception.

If a wild knockout happens while scouting a pivot, you must replace the runner with a catch from that area before leaving or healing. Do not just keep the gained experience.

kaizo_moves.title: Kaizo: moves and abilities
kaizo_moves.text:
Use naturally learned moves and the TMs awarded directly by Gym Leaders. Ordinary found TMs and general tutors are not a free move pool.

Healing moves, including draining attacks, Leech Seed, status-healing moves and similar recovery, are banned. Spore and Assist are also banned. HM moves remain banned in battle.

Banned moves have a lab-fight exception. After leaving the lab, a recovery move is not legal merely because your HP is already full.

Metronome and temporarily copied moves have their published exceptions. Do not turn that into permission to learn and repeatedly use a normally banned move.

With Huge Power or Pure Power, physical attacks are restricted unless the low-BST exception applies: 399 BST or less, or 400 to 410 inclusive while the Pokemon can still evolve.

Those ability limits have a lab exception too. Afterward, use legal moves or pivot. In Classic, physical follows type. In Modern, read the move's category.

Do not re-teach Sketch to repeatedly copy new moves. Baconmon's TM-paid reminder does not remove that restriction.

kaizo_items.title: Kaizo: items and healing
kaizo_items.text:
Outside battle, do not use items that restore HP, status or PP. PP Up and PP Max are treated separately by Kaizo; stricter variants can limit them further.

Most permanent held items are not allowed. The normal allowed groups are consumable-on-use items, necessary evolution items while evolving, and Smoke Ball. Apply the published item bans and lab exceptions.

Do not use coloured flutes to bypass the status-healing restriction. A reusable healing effect is still healing.

Do not use optional healing stations inside a dungeon. A bed or NPC doing the same job as a Pokemon Center is included. Mandatory story healing is a separate case.

A legal Center visit outside a dungeon is allowed in ordinary Kaizo. Survival adds its own limited-heal budget.

Found items are not a licence to farm a respawn. Guaranteed hidden-item spawns in this ROM make access reliable; they do not let you repeatedly harvest the same spot.

kaizo_route.title: Kaizo: route and dungeon plan
kaizo_route.text:
Fight each trainer only once. Do not use the VS Seeker to add training battles. Avoid wild experience except for the precise published exceptions.

Enter a gym or dojo prepared to finish every trainer without leaving. For other dungeons, plan your one visit and the fights you will take.

The standard Kaizo rule does not award points. VS and Baconmon add bonuses for full clears. A partial visit can forfeit a bonus even if you never return.

Do not leave, heal and then continue the same clear. Do not replace the outside heal with an internal bed. The score log checks both problems in its five bonus dungeons.

FireRed's ship rival must be fought first. The first Lavender visit has its tower-rival requirement. Story-required returns do not authorize general healing or farming.

Randomize ordinary trainers and wild Pokemon with a 50% level boost. Do not increase static encounter levels. Force trainer Pokemon fully evolved from level 30, add three Pokemon to boss teams, and leave easier evolutions disabled. Follow the FireRed preset for the remaining settings.

A plain unrandomized BASE ROM is not a valid Kaizo seed. Baconmon normalizes the lab rival to level 8 even if another randomizer pass alters that specific level.

kaizo_clauses.title: Kaizo: declared exceptions
kaizo_clauses.text:
In published Ironmon, favourite Pokemon are declared before play, not picked from whatever the starter screen happens to show. The legendary allowance is limited too.

Declare at most one nemesis species before the run. You may knock it out in the wild once per run, but you may never catch it as a pivot. Evolving into it is allowed.

In ordinary Kaizo, if the nemesis appears in the lab, take the starter that would face it, provided that starter is legal. A declared favourite takes priority. If the other two starters are both banned, take the nemesis. Baconmon keeps its preselected ball instead of using that starter-selection override.

Ironmon's shiny allowance concerns a bonus knockout. Do not import a Nuzlocke shiny-catch clause without saying you changed the rules.

Baconmon's fixed starter ball replaces choosing a ball after the reveal. It does not add favourite or nemesis exceptions that let you abandon your fixed position.

If you choose to play the published Kaizo format instead, follow its exact starter and clause rules. Label the run accurately and agree on the format before comparing results.

iron_vs.title: Ironmon VS
iron_vs.text:
Ironmon VS turns Kaizo progress into a team points race. Teams play matching seeds, assign starter positions and share information learned through play.

The official extension is by WaffleSmacker. The challenge inherits iateyourpie's Ironmon rules. The public VS site supplies the score schedule used here.

VS lowers the lab rival to level 6, gives one Master Ball plus five Poke Balls, and rotates the early pivot encounters. Its starter-slot exception permits the Pokemon in the assigned ball.

Log viewing during the run is banned. Team information is learned through gameplay, not by reading the seed's spoiler file.

The full score is 33: nine from gyms, thirteen from the Elite Four and Champion, and eleven from the five dungeon bonuses. See Score rules for each award.

Agree on any extra changes before a competition.

iron_survival.title: Survival Ironmon
iron_survival.text:
Survival adds a limited Pokemon Center budget and resource trades to inherited Kaizo rules. It is a separate published ruleset, not merely Kaizo with fewer Potions.

The general budget is ten voluntary Center-equivalent heals after the opening grace period, with an extra one after badge eight. Optional dungeon healers remain banned.

The format has an early twenty-Potion purchase allowance and its own PP Up, PP Max and flute trade rules. Those allowances do not carry into ordinary Kaizo or Baconmon by default.

Different games have further changes. Check the current Survival section and the game's settings sheet before using an allowance.

Keep a separate record of your Survival heal budget, and use the required Survival settings.

iron_super.title: Super Kaizo
iron_super.text:
Super Kaizo is iateyourpie's harder variation. Use the rules and patches from PyroMikeGit's Super Kaizo project.

Its extra rules include smarter trainer AI, a required mid-game pivot and restrictions on things such as early hidden items, setup and strong defensive abilities.

The FireRed rules also change progression and limit ship battles. Those changes conflict with ordinary VS's full S.S. Anne bonus plan.

Do not score a Super Kaizo attempt against Baconmon's 33-point board as though the same opportunities were available.

iron_plus.title: Kaizo Ironmon Plus
iron_plus.text:
Kaizo Ironmon+, by Corvimae, is a separate rebalance built around the physical/special split.

Use that project's rules, patch and randomizer settings to play it. Baconmon Modern follows the changes listed in its own mode pages.

iron_doubles.title: Kaizo Doubles
iron_doubles.text:
Kaizo Doubles is a variation with two runners and doubled trainer battles. Losing either runner ends that format's run.

Its pivot and shared-move restrictions are different from single-runner Kaizo. It needs the correct doubles randomizer setup.

Having an occasional double battle in FireRed is not the same as turning every possible trainer battle into doubles.

iron_rogue.title: Roguemon and other formats
iron_rogue.text:
Roguemon is an Ironmon extension by something-smart, with events, rewards and progression systems. Follow its installation instructions and rules to play it.

Subpar and Soft Kaizo are other community variations. Pick the version you want and read its rules before starting.

If you combine rules from several challenges, write down your changes before the run.

score_rules.title: 33-point scoring
score_rules.text:
Brock is worth 2 points. Each of the other seven Gym Leaders is worth 1. All eight gyms together give 9.

Lorelei, Bruno, Agatha and Lance are worth 2 each. The Champion is worth 5. That gives 13 more, for 22 before dungeon bonuses.

Full Mt. Moon gives 1. Full S.S. Anne gives 1. Full Rock Tunnel gives 1. Full Silph Co. gives 3. Full Victory Road gives 5. Those eleven bonus points bring the maximum to 33.

The lab rival, Rocket Hideout, Pokemon Tower and Pokemon Mansion do not have extra awards in this score schedule.

Defeat every required trainer group. Starter-dependent rival teams are alternatives: you need your seed's actual rival, not all three possible versions.

An award is recorded once. Re-entering an area, reopening this item or loading a normal save does not award it again.

score_clean.title: Clean full clears
score_clean.text:
The bonus visit starts when you enter the dungeon. Internal floors and connected rooms remain one area for this purpose.

Clear every required trainer before leaving. Leaving early forfeits the bonus. Coming back and finishing the checklist does not make the original visit clean.

No Pokemon Center or equivalent heal during that visit. The Silph bed and S.S. Anne healer are included. In-battle items used within the rules are not Center heals.

If a full heal is used inside a monitored dungeon, its bonus is removed or blocked even when every trainer flag is set. The run log marks that problem.

If you leave an incomplete dungeon, the log marks its bonus forfeited. Re-entering to continue it marks a one-visit rule break. Healing outside and returning cannot clear that mark.

Completing a dungeon and then leaving to heal is fine for its earned clear. Other Kaizo rules still govern later revisits and optional healing.

score_limits.title: What the score log can know
score_limits.text:
The log starts recording visits when it's first used. An older save doesn't say which healers you visited beforehand.

Past dungeons with trainer wins are marked Unverified. You'll still see your Gym and League points. Unvisited dungeons can earn clean-clear bonuses as usual.

The log watches the five scoring dungeons. You're responsible for catches, moves, held items, starter-ball choice and the rest of your rules.

This item keeps the current run's score and dungeon-clear log.

Save normally after progress. Restoring an earlier save also restores its earlier score and visit history.

score_gym.title: Gym and League values
score_gym.text:
Brock: 2. Misty: 1. Lt. Surge: 1. Erika: 1. Koga: 1. Sabrina: 1. Blaine: 1. Giovanni at the gym: 1.

Lorelei: 2. Bruno: 2. Agatha: 2. Lance: 2. Champion: 5.

The guide checks the corresponding trainer victory flags, including the alternative Champion teams. It does not add the same reward for a rematch.

Losing your runner still ends a Kaizo attempt. A points total is a progress record, not permission to continue a dead run as though it were valid.

rom_features.title: About this ROM
rom_features.text:
Kaizo Baconmon. Developed by xbaconator9000x.

A FireRed Kaizo Ironmon hack based on Faster FireRed and Ironmon VS, with a few changes to make runs less fiddly.

Choose your gender, name and rival's name, then start in Oak's lab. Pick Classic or Modern battle rules. Your rival's starter is level 8 in either mode.

You get a Master Ball and five Poke Balls early on. Early encounters rotate as they do in Ironmon VS.

Use field HMs without teaching them. You still need the HM, badge and usual story requirements. Fly from the Town Map. Rock Tunnel stays lit.

The lab machine sets your lead Pokemon's friendship to maximum or minimum. The former friendship helpers point you to the lab machine. The forest nurse heals you even if you're poisoned.

The Fuchsia Move Reminder shares a house with the Move Deleter. He charges one TM for each move you successfully relearn.

Renewable hidden items appear at every normal refresh. Kaizo's ban on farming them still applies.

Press L while choosing an attack to read its description. Move summaries show physical, special and status symbols. Nuz-guide has the rules, current score and dungeon-clear log.

rom_foundation.title: Thanks and credits
rom_foundation.text:
Developed by xbaconator9000x.

Faster FireRed by DrMaple supplies the faster opening and field conveniences. Baconmon starts directly in Oak's lab.

Ironmon VS provides the main rules and scoring reference. The official tracker extension is by WaffleSmacker.

Ironmon was created by iateyourpie. Thanks to valiant-code and UTDZac for the rules and randomizer settings, and pret for the FireRed engine reference.

rom_changes.title: Foundational changelog
rom_changes.text:
v0.9.3: Friendship changes now use Oak's lab machine exclusively. The lab aide and both Viridian helpers point you there.

Nuz-guide: rules, challenge variations, credits, current score and saved dungeon-clear checks.

Town Map Fly: selecting an unlocked town starts the flight and takes you there. Works from the Bag or registered-item shortcut.

New game: choose your gender, name and rival's name before starting in the lab.

Lab machine: maximum friendship, minimum friendship or Cancel. It affects the lead Pokemon.

Battle information: L opens move descriptions. Category symbols appear in move summaries.

Classic or Modern: choose the original battle rules or the move split and updated existing abilities.

Other changes: Grumpig title screen, early balls, rotating early encounters, field HMs without teaching, lit Rock Tunnel, friendship helpers, poison-friendly forest nurse and a TM-paid Fuchsia Move Reminder.

The opening rival is level 8 in both modes.

rom_randomizer.title: Randomizing this ROM
rom_randomizer.text:
Randomize BASE with the Kaizo FireRed preset. BASE itself is not a randomized Kaizo seed.

The opening rival stays at level 8, even after randomization. Other trainer levels follow the preset.

Keep the boss-party, forced-evolution and other settings required by Kaizo. Modern changes battles; it does not choose randomizer settings for you.

Don't randomize an already randomized seed. Keep its log for after the run, and don't read it during a blind VS attempt.

When updating an existing run, use the matching current-run ROM and save normally first. Keep a backup of your ROM and save.

rom_limits.title: Limits and other challenges
rom_limits.text:
Choose a ruleset before starting and stick to it. Helpers and items can still be banned by the challenge you're playing.

Nuz-guide keeps track of progress. It doesn't stop you making illegal catches or using banned moves and items. Fainted Pokemon must still be boxed or released according to your rules.

Modern keeps the Gen III Pokemon, moves, abilities and seed data. Read the mode pages for the battle changes.

Save normally to keep your score and visit history. Loading an earlier save takes those records back too.

credits_project.title: Kaizo Baconmon
credits_project.text:
Developed by xbaconator9000x.

Kaizo Baconmon is my take on Kaizo Ironmon, based mainly on Ironmon VS. I wanted the same challenge with less time spent on HM friends, friendship and other busywork.

Classic keeps the old battle rules. Modern adds the move split and updates abilities already in Gen III. Pick whichever you prefer and use the same mode when comparing runs.

Thanks to the Ironmon community and everyone behind the tools and hacks listed in the credits. Have fun, and try to get out of the lab.

bacon_setup.title: Seed and battle setup
bacon_setup.text:
Randomize Pokemon species, abilities, stat spreads, learnsets, trainer teams, wild encounters and items with the FireRed Kaizo preset. Use a new seed after each loss. Keep the same declared starter ball between runs.

Boost ordinary trainer and wild levels by 50%. Do not boost static encounter levels. Force trainer Pokemon to be fully evolved from level 30. Add three Pokemon to boss teams. Use Fluctuating growth for ordinary Pokemon and Slow growth for legendaries. Leave easier evolutions disabled. Randomize Pickup items with bad items excluded. Use the complete FireRed preset for the other randomizer options.

Choose Classic or Modern before the run and keep it for the whole attempt. Use Set battle style. Speed controls are allowed; undoing outcomes with save states is not.

You begin in Oak's lab after choosing your gender, name and rival name. You do not need to leave the lab to talk to Mom. The opening rival is level 8 in either mode. Fight the opening battle even if you dislike your starter.

You receive one Master Ball and five Poke Balls early. They are legal to use for catches that obey the catch rules. A Master Ball does not make an otherwise illegal pivot legal.

bacon_selection.title: Starter and species limits
bacon_selection.text:
Choose left, middle or right before seeing any starter options. Keep that position across attempts. Do not inspect the choices and switch balls. In a VS event, agree on ball positions before anyone reveals the starters.

The Pokemon in your fixed ball is legal regardless of BST. This is only a BST exception: the move, ability and held-item restrictions still apply after the lab battle.

For wild pivots, 599 BST or higher is banned. Legendary and mythical Pokemon are banned except for at most one predeclared favourite, which must be below 600 BST. Declare up to three favourite species before starting; this list never overrides Baconmon's fixed starter ball. It does not remove the level, route or catch restrictions.

An evolution is allowed to take your legal runner above the BST limit or into a legendary species. You must let every evolution happen. Do not cancel it or use an Everstone. Catching an already over-limit wild Pokemon is not the same as evolving into it.

There is no starter reroll for a bad ability or moveset. Use the lab exceptions, then avoid prohibited actions or pivot. If your runner has no legal way to continue, the run is over.

bacon_catches.title: Runner, catches and pivots
bacon_catches.text:
Use one Pokemon in battle. No backups, switching between runners, sacrifice Pokemon or extra party abilities. This ROM does not need HM friends. Do not keep extra Pokemon for Pickup, weather, item bonuses or any other advantage.

Obtain no more than six Pokemon during the run, counting your starter and accepted pivots. You may accept at most one Pokemon from each named route or area. It need not be the first encounter. Gifts and static encounters also use that area's allowance. Separate floors of one named dungeon do not create extra catches.

A catch may be at most four levels above your current runner. Commit to a pivot when you catch it, before examining its stats, moves or ability. Permanently retire the old runner; you cannot return to it later. Do not catch several candidates and compare them.

You may immediately box an unwanted catch without viewing any stats or moves and continue as if it had not been accepted. This is not permission to scout caught Pokemon or use a second battler. Throwing a ball to escape a dangerous wild encounter is allowed.

Do not deliberately knock out wild Pokemon for experience. Scout or run instead. A wild Pokemon destroying itself is not deliberate training. If you accidentally knock one out while scouting, you must pivot to a legal catch from that area before leaving or healing. If that cannot be done legally, the run cannot continue.

bacon_clauses.title: Shinies, nemesis and losses
bacon_clauses.text:
You may defeat a wild shiny as a bonus knockout. Do not raise the shiny rate. This is not an extra catch allowance or permission to replace your fixed starter ball.

You may declare one nemesis species before playing. Once per run, you may deliberately defeat it in the wild. You may never catch it as a pivot. Evolving into it is allowed. Baconmon's fixed ball takes priority over ordinary Kaizo's nemesis-based starter selection.

Your runner fainting ends the attempt, including poison damage outside battle. Do not revive it, continue with a backup or recover its held item for another runner. Begin again on a newly randomized seed.

Save normally to stop playing and continue later. Save states may be used as a suspension tool only if they do not undo outcomes or reveal information you then act on in an earlier state. No resets for better damage rolls, encounters, catches or rewards.

Each trainer can be defeated once. No VS Seeker grinding. Collect each renewable item location once; do not farm respawning hidden items. Guaranteed hidden-item appearances change availability, not that restriction.

bacon_moves.title: Moves, TMs and abilities
bacon_moves.text:
Use moves learned naturally by level or evolution, and compatible TMs handed to you directly for beating Gym Leaders. Ordinary found, bought or held TMs cannot be taught. General move tutors are banned.

Baconmon allows the Fuchsia Move Reminder in the Move Deleter's house. Pay one TM of your choice for each successfully remembered move. The payment TM's move is irrelevant. Cancelling or having no eligible move costs nothing. HMs cannot be payment. Do not relearn Sketch after that Pokemon has already used it to copy a move.

The following Gen III moves are banned in battle: Cut, Fly, Surf, Strength, Flash, Rock Smash, Waterfall and Dive; Spore and Assist; Absorb, Mega Drain, Giga Drain, Leech Life, Dream Eater, Leech Seed, Recover, Soft-Boiled, Rest, Milk Drink, Morning Sun, Synthesis, Moonlight, Wish, Slack Off, Ingrain, Swallow, Pain Split, Heal Bell, Aromatherapy and Refresh.

Do not use any other HP-restoring, draining or status-curing move if a modified seed includes one. Banned moves are still banned at full HP. Metronome may call one, and Mimic may temporarily copy and use one for that battle. Those exceptions do not let you permanently learn a banned move.

Huge Power and Pure Power prohibit physical attacks unless the Pokemon has 399 BST or less, or 400 to 410 BST inclusive and can still evolve. Special attacks remain legal. In Classic, category follows type; in Modern, use the move's physical or special icon.

The initial lab battle allows otherwise banned moves, abilities and held items. Once it ends, remove banned held items and stop using banned moves or prohibited physical attacks. Pivot if you cannot continue legally.

bacon_items.title: Items, shops and stealing
bacon_items.text:
Only buy Poke Balls and Repels, including their different varieties. You may sell items. Do not buy healing items, vitamins, TMs, held items or other supplies. Do not ask an NPC to shop for you, or buy legal items to trade for prohibited supplies.

Use found or NPC-given items subject to the bans below. Lucky Egg and Sacred Ash are banned. Leftovers, Soul Dew and Everstone are banned. Focus Sash is banned if present. Do not use coloured flutes to cure status.

Allowed held items are items consumed when they activate, such as berries, Berry Juice and White Herb; items held solely for a required evolution; and Smoke Ball. Other permanent held items, including damage boosters and healing items, are banned. The initial lab battle is the held-item exception.

Do not intentionally steal wild held items with Thief, Covet or similar effects. If you accidentally take an item from a wild Pokemon you do not catch, discard it. Stealing from trainers is allowed, but you must remove a prohibited held item after the battle.

Using a found item does not waive the healing rules. The TM-paid Move Reminder is an express trade exception: you may spend an otherwise unusable TM there, but not buy TMs to supply him.

bacon_progress.title: FireRed route and helper rules
bacon_progress.text:
On the S.S. Anne, fight the rival before any other ship trainer. On your first visit to Lavender Town, fight the Pokemon Tower rival before leaving town; return later with the Silph Scope for story progression. Do not travel to the Sevii Islands with Bill before beating the Elite Four.

The lab machine may set your runner's friendship to 255 or 0. Using it is allowed in Baconmon. The former friendship NPCs now point you to that machine and do not change friendship themselves.

Field HMs need their normal HM, badge and location or story prerequisites. Your runner need not learn the move, and no HM friend is required. Use the Town Map outdoors to Fly to an unlocked destination with HM02 and the Thunder Badge.

Cut needs Cascade; Fly needs Thunder; Surf needs Soul; Strength needs Rainbow; Flash needs Boulder; Rock Smash needs Marsh; Waterfall needs Volcano. Rock Tunnel is already lit. HMs are still banned as battle moves.

The tracker may record observed moves, abilities, notes, encounters, ratings, cards and progress. These are aids, not extra catches or battle permissions. Review unrevealed seed details only after your run ends; do not consult the randomizer's spoiler log during an active attempt.

The challenge ends when you beat the Champion and enter the Hall of Fame. A score record does not excuse a rule breach. All the rules above still apply if the game or tracker lets you perform an illegal action.

bacon_changes.title: Core changes
bacon_changes.text:
I implemented the following changes from core Kaizo Ironmon:

- Start in Oak's lab after choosing your gender, name and rival's name. The opening rival battle still happens at level 8.

- Choose Classic or Modern at the start. Classic keeps Gen III battles. Modern adds the physical/special move split and updates existing abilities. It does not add abilities, learnsets or BST changes.

- Pick a starter ball before seeing the choices and keep that same position across runs. Your chosen starter is legal regardless of BST. This replaces normal starter selection. It does not allow over-limit wild pivots.

- Start with a Master Ball and five Poke Balls for legal catches.

- Early encounters rotate as they do in Ironmon VS.

- Use field HMs without teaching them or carrying an HM friend. You still need the HM, badge and normal story prerequisites. Fly from the Town Map.

- Rock Tunnel is already lit, so you do not need Flash to see there.

- Use the Move Reminder in the Move Deleter's Fuchsia house. Each successful relearn costs one TM of your choice. The usual Sketch restriction still applies.

- Use Oak's lab machine to maximise or plummet your runner's friendship. The former friendship helpers point you there.

- Use the Viridian Forest nurse even when poisoned. Dungeon beds and other optional dungeon healers remain banned.

- Chance-based hidden items are guaranteed to appear at their normal refresh. Collect each renewable location once; farming is still banned.

- Track progress with the 33-point VS-style score and dungeon-clear log. A dungeon bonus requires all its trainers in one visit without optional Center-equivalent healing.

- Press L while choosing an attack to read its description. Move summaries show physical, special and status symbols.

- A Baconmon title screen starring Grumpig.

- Start with Nuz-guide: the complete Baconmon rules, other challenge formats, mode details, scoring, credits and ROM information.

Everything else follows the full Kaizo Baconmon rules in this guide. Built-in conveniences do not waive the remaining restrictions.

bacon_goal.title: Goal and run rules
bacon_goal.text:
Reach the Hall of Fame with one surviving runner. A fainted runner ends the run. Start the next attempt on a newly randomized seed. Do not reload to undo a loss, bad catch, move choice or other result.

The Full rules pages include the inherited Standard, Ultimate and Kaizo restrictions with the Baconmon changes applied. Read both rules menus, the battle mode pages and the point rules. You do not need to combine rules from the other challenge directories.

Agree on the same mode, starter-ball assignments and rules before a VS run. All restrictions still apply when the game or tracker allows an illegal action.
